clue.text: Drink amid hubbub one rejected, lacking interest

indicators.note: amid means the drink sits in the middle of the other letters
rejected means the hubbub and the one are turned back to front

parts.note: a hubbub is a din
one is the Roman numeral I
to drink is to sip

explanation.surface: Someone has a drink in the middle of a noisy crowd and finds it all dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns DIN + I into INID, and 'amid' puts SIP into its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid things are bland and dull, without flavour or anything to hold attention.

clue.text: Moment with judge not appearing to be doubtful

indicators.note: not appearing means the judge's letter is left out

parts.note: a jiffy is a moment

explanation.surface: A judge fails to turn up for a moment, which looks suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: Iffy is informal for uncertain or dubious, a synonym of doubtful.

clue.text: Powder lay around plant

indicators.note: around means the word for lay goes outside the plant

parts.note: to lay something down is to set it
a herb is a plant

explanation.surface: A gardener sprinkles powder around a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Sherbet in Britain is a fizzy sweet powder eaten as confectionery.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage, sherbet is a sweet effervescent powder, sold as a children's confection.

clue.text: Quiet dog sadly over year getting fat

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the earlier letters sit above the year

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quiet

indicators.note: sadly means the letters of dog are in a poor state, rearranged

explanation.surface: A subdued dog, sad as the year goes on, is putting on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Podgy means short and plump, a synonym of fat.

clue.text: Perform little around country

parts.note: to do is to perform
mini means small or little
CA, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: Putting on a short show here and there across the land.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominica is an island nation in the Caribbean, an example of a country.

clue.text: Bidding millions, fellow admitted to hoax

indicators.note: admitted to means these letters are let inside the hoax word

parts.note: cod is an old word for a hoax or a joke
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone bidding millions at an auction turns out to be part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidding is an order or instruction, the same as a command given to someone.

clue.text: Building opening for visitors to view features

definitions.text: Building opening for visitors to view features

parts.words: Building opening for visitors to view features
parts.note: read as a stately home welcoming tourists to admire its architectural details, but features are feature films shown in a building for that

explanation.definitionFit: A cinema is a building where audiences watch feature films, which are called features.

clue.text: Preserve horse, disease mostly contained

indicators.note: contained means the horse holds the disease inside

parts.note: a mare is a female horse

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for disease is dropped

parts.note: a malady is a disease

explanation.surface: A horse kept in quarantine, with the illness largely confined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb at the head of the clue, but it is the noun for a jar of fruit spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus jam, an example of a preserve.

clue.text: Bowl over area with dust on ground

indicators.note: ground, as in ground down, means the letters of dust on are crushed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A field covered in dust bowls someone over.
explanation.definitionFit: To bowl someone over is to astonish them, an idiom with the same meaning.

clue.text: Saint imprisoned by dreadful cult, imbued with power, showing scorn

indicators.note: imprisoned by means the saint is locked inside the word for dreadful

parts.note: dire means dreadful

indicators.note: imbued with means the cult takes the power inside it

parts.note: a sect is a cult

explanation.surface: A holy man jailed by a terrible, powerful sect is treated with contempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Disrespect is a lack of regard, close in meaning to scorn or contempt.

clue.text: Revolutionary provided with award for service in dash for cover?

indicators.note: revolutionary means the word for provided is turned round

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided that'

indicators.note: in means the award sits inside the word for dash

parts.note: dash, meaning flair or panache, is elan
the DSM is the Distinguished Service Medal

explanation.surface: A rebel is decorated for running for shelter in some military action.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a fielding position in cricket, so the question mark flags that a player stationed there is meant; 'Revolutionary' turns IF into FI.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, cover is a fielding position, and a player stationed there is one example of a fielder.

clue.text: Formal procedures necessary to inherit estate

indicators.note: necessary to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Legal formalities must be gone through before you can come into a property.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are ceremonies, set forms of words and actions, so formal procedures fits as a synonym.

clue.text: Governor, mad one, in error? Yes, to a massive extent

parts.note: a bey was a governor of a province in the Ottoman Empire

indicators.note: in error means the letters of mad one are muddled

parts.note: sure is an informal way of saying yes

explanation.surface: A provincial ruler who is crazy gets things wrong and admits it hugely.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done beyond measure is done immeasurably, hence to a massive extent: an idiom of degree.

clue.text: Result of interlacing affection in chapter with irritation

indicators.note: in means the affection goes inside the chapter abbreviation

parts.note: love is affection
an itch is an irritation

explanation.surface: A love affair in a book's chapter leads to annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: A clove hitch is a knot used to fasten a rope to a post.
explanation.definitionFit: A clove hitch is a knot, which is what interlacing a rope produces.

clue.text: Writer's skill kindled ecstasy, full of vigour

parts.note: kindled means set alight, lit
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
racy can mean lively and spirited

explanation.surface: An author's talent stirred readers to rapture, bursting with energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the ability to read and write, a basic skill of any writer.

clue.text: Updated supervisor of play concerning cast

parts.note: a ref, a referee, supervises play in a game
re means concerning
to cast skin or leaves is to shed them

explanation.surface: A theatre director revises the play, mindful of the actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' and 'cast' suggest a theatre, but the play is a game supervised by a referee.
explanation.definitionFit: Refreshed can mean brought up to date, as a refreshed web page is updated.

clue.text: Fully committed assistance received by young boxer?

indicators.note: received by means the assistance goes inside the young boxer

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, so a young one is a pup
assistance is aid

explanation.surface: A dedicated trainer helps out a novice fighter in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' suggests a fighter, but the question mark hints at the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A paid-up member has paid all dues, so figuratively someone wholly committed to a cause.

clue.text: Boat in old drama sheltered by promontory

indicators.note: sheltered by means the inner letters are tucked inside the promontory

parts.note: a mull is a Scottish promontory, as in the Mull of Kintyre
Noh is classical Japanese drama

explanation.surface: A vessel features in a period play staged beneath a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A monohull is a boat with a single hull, as opposed to a catamaran.

clue.text: Strong criticism against coming back with variable support

parts.note: V is short for versus, against

indicators.note: coming back means the word for strong criticism is read backwards

parts.note: to come under fire is to face strong criticism
Y is a conventional algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Harsh disapproval returns, propped up by changing evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the criticism before 'against', yet the V for 'against' leads the answer, because a charade is assembled in answer order.
explanation.definitionFit: To verify a claim is to confirm it, lending it support with evidence.

clue.text: Whale in river followed by men with uneasy feeling, mostly

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers, men

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the uneasy feeling is dropped

parts.note: a qualm is an uneasy feeling

explanation.surface: Sailors on a river spot a whale and feel rather nervous.
explanation.definitionFit: A rorqual is a type of baleen whale, such as the blue whale or fin whale.

clue.text: Quarrel monk cites, getting out of order

parts.note: Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

indicators.note: getting out of order means the letters of cites are jumbled

explanation.surface: A monk quotes texts in the wrong sequence and an argument starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting out of order' turns CITES into ESTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A domestic is British informal for a household row, especially between partners.

clue.text: Slip up after thaw's beginning on great street

indicators.note: after means the slip comes after that first letter
in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece
beginning means the first letter of thaw is taken

parts.note: to slip up is to err
ace means great or excellent

explanation.surface: Someone slips as the ice starts melting on a grand road.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of joined houses, and so a street name in Britain.

clue.text: Old-fashioned enclosure occupied by bird? Not right

indicators.note: occupied by means the enclosure has the bird inside it

parts.note: a sty is an enclosure for pigs

indicators.note: not right means the R for right is removed

parts.note: a ruff is a wading bird

explanation.surface: A pen with a bird in it seems rather dated, but is it wrong?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the bird being a wader rather than anything kept in a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffy describes people or attitudes that are staid, conventional and old-fashioned.

clue.text: Allotted place held by one who's idolised more than president

indicators.note: held by means the allotted place sits inside the idol

parts.note: someone idolised is a hero
a berth is a place allotted, for a ship or sleeper
over means more than

explanation.surface: A reserved seat is kept by someone worshipped even more than the head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: This man was the thirty-first President of the United States, from 1929 to 1933.

clue.text: Provider of cross helping contest's top scorer to get goal?

definitions.text: Provider of cross helping contest's top scorer to get goal?

parts.words: Provider of cross helping contest's top scorer to get goal?
parts.note: read as a football winger crossing for a striker, but the cross is an X on a ballot paper helping the election's top candidate win

explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks a cross on a ballot, helping the candidate with most votes win the seat.

clue.text: Group drinking session being reported

indicators.note: being reported means the word for a drinking session is heard spoken

parts.note: a bevvy is British slang for a drinking session

explanation.surface: A gang of friends have a night out drinking, and it gets reported.
explanation.walkthrough: Bevvy is British slang for a drink or a boozy session.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a group, especially of birds or people, a collective noun.

clue.text: Move tons with expression of pain

parts.note: ouch is what you cry when hurt

explanation.surface: Shifting heavy weights makes someone cry out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To move someone emotionally is to touch them, a synonym in the sense of stirring feeling.

clue.text: Stop being animated after eating fungus

indicators.note: eating means the shuffled letters take in the fungus
being animated means the letters of after are set in motion and rearranged

parts.note: rust is a fungal disease of plants

explanation.surface: Someone stops being lively once they have eaten a mushroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' looks like a link word placing the eating in time, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To frustrate a plan is to thwart it, bringing it to a stop.

clue.text: Call for attention to bandage covering a break

indicators.note: to bandage means to wrap round, so the call encloses the other letters

parts.note: hoy is a shout to attract attention
a lid is a covering

explanation.surface: Someone shouts for help to dress a wound over a fracture.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical picture makes 'break' look like a fracture, but it is a break from work.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a break from work or school, a period of rest.

clue.text: In the main US city bank, put about 1000 dollars

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

indicators.note: put about means the word for bank is placed around the thousand

parts.note: to bank on is to rely
G, a grand, is slang for a thousand dollars

explanation.surface: A Los Angeles bank deposits about a thousand dollars, mostly.
explanation.definitionFit: In the main and largely are both adverbs meaning for the most part, so they are synonyms.
